previousCurrentEvent.label: Milngin Ward replacement by-election
previousCurrentEvent.dateBasis: NTEC’s current candidate list and closure notice, both updated 20 November and read 21 November, confirm two nominees for one vacancy and a contested election. The updated timetable starts mobile voting at 9 am on 23 November and early voting at 8:30 am on 30 November. Election day starts at 8 am on 3 December; counting starts at 6 pm. Result declaration is scheduled for 10 am on 17 December. The summary labels 29 November and 1 December at 6 pm as postal dispatch cutoffs. Existing early-voting/polling closing times and postal application/receipt deadlines retain their 14 November evidence; those fields were not reverified by this summary. The Australia/Darwin (ACST) timezone also retains its earlier evidence; the updated HTML does not print a timezone.
previousCurrentEvent.contestantNote: NTEC declares two nominees for one councillor vacancy. Display names follow the current candidate list. The closure notice lists ballot order but spells the first surname McTahhart, while the candidate list spells it MCTAGGART; this source discrepancy is retained. Affiliations are not supplied and are not inferred.

previousNtStateData.name: Northern Territory
previousNtStateData.researchStatus: Scoped 21 November Milngin review: NTEC’s current candidate list and closure notice confirm two nominees for one vacancy and a contested election. The current timetable starts mobile voting at 9 am on 23 November and early voting at 8:30 am on 30 November. Earlier 14 November evidence is retained for early voting close at 6 pm on 2 December, overseas/local postal application deadlines at 6 pm on 29 November/1 December, election-day voting close at 6 pm on 3 December and completed ballots due by noon on 16 December. Those closing/application/receipt deadlines were not reverified today. The updated timetable instead labels 29 November and 1 December as postal dispatch cutoffs. It schedules election-day start at 8 am on 3 December, counting at 6 pm and result declaration at 10 am on 17 December. Australia/Darwin (ACST) remains the earlier reviewed timezone; the updated HTML does not print a timezone. Parliament retains its 23 October review: September official roster reconciles 25 MLAs, 17 CLP, 6 Labor and 2 independents; Johnston identity join corrected and Mulka/Nightcliff results retained separately. Other council coverage remains partial; federal profiles were inaccessible in the prior review.

strategyNotes: The NT page is a compact chamber model with a very large government majority.
The recent Nightcliff by-election shows how a single seat can change the story of a small parliament.
Future updates should watch local issues, not just party totals, because every electorate has outsized weight.
